periodicity.text: The light curve is dominated by a smooth sinusoid with period 0.17134 d (Lomb-Scargle power 0.56); the adopted 0.68440 d is 3.99 x that. The true period is more likely 0.17134 d (pulsation or spots) or 0.34268 d (contact binary), and the 'eclipses' may not be eclipses.

writeup: TIC 251077178 is a candidate eclipsing binary star with an orbital period of 0.6844 days. TESS photometry reveals a primary eclipse causing a 2.74% dimming of the star's light, detected with a signal-to-noise ratio of 319.2 using the Box Least Squares method. No secondary eclipse was detected. Pixel-level image analysis provides supporting evidence, with a difference-imaging peak signal-to-noise of 14.2, though the centroid offset of 2.2 arcsec from the target warrants consideration. The candidate does not appear in six major variable-star catalogs, suggesting it may be previously unknown. The pipeline's machine learning classifier assigned this target a score of 0.82, indicating high confidence in its reality as a stellar system. This candidate passed all automated data quality checks.
